citation: B. Pasca, "High-Performance Floating-Point Computing on Reconfigurable Circuits", PhD thesis, ENS Lyon, 2011
title: High-performance floating-point computing on reconfigurable circuits

segments.title: Front matter
segments.why: The front matter contains publication metadata and acknowledgements rather than arithmetic-unit design detail.

segments.title: Introduction
segments.why: The introduction motivates FPGA computing and application parallelism without describing an arithmetic-unit mechanism.

segments.title: Field Programmable Gate Arrays
segments.why: The chapter surveys FPGA carry hardware and embedded multiplier/DSP resources that determine arithmetic-unit implementations.

segments.title: Floating-point arithmetic
segments.why: The chapter defines floating-point formats and numerical semantics without presenting a hardware mechanism.

segments.title: Custom arithmetic data-path design
segments.why: The chapter concerns arithmetic-library/HLS workflows and the FloPoCo framework rather than a specific arithmetic-unit architecture.

segments.title: Binary addition in FloPoCo
segments.why: The chapter compares FPGA carry-propagation and segmented short-latency adder architectures and evaluates their frequency/resource tradeoffs.

segments.title: Large multipliers with fewer DSP blocks
segments.why: The chapter develops operand-decomposition algorithms that reduce the DSP-block count of large exact multipliers.

segments.title: Polynomial-based architectures for function evaluation
segments.why: The chapter defines FPGA function evaluators built from segmented polynomial approximations, coefficient tables, Horner evaluation, and truncated arithmetic.

segments.title: Multiplicative square root algorithms
segments.why: The chapter compares digit-recurrence and multiplier-based square-root units and develops a polynomial-approximation implementation.

segments.title: Floating-point exponential
segments.why: The chapter compares table/CORDIC exponential units and develops a floating-point exponential architecture using range reduction and polynomial evaluation.

segments.title: Floating-point accumulation and sum-of-products
segments.why: The chapter develops fixed-point-window floating-point accumulators and sum-of-products units that defer normalization and improve accumulation accuracy.

segments.title: High-level synthesis of perfect loop nests
segments.why: The chapter concerns compiler scheduling and high-level synthesis of loop nests rather than arithmetic-unit microarchitecture.

segments.title: Using FloPoCo to solve Table Maker’s Dilemma
segments.why: The chapter develops an FPGA-based search for hardest-to-round cases that determines the precision required by correctly rounded elementary-function units.

segments.title: Conclusions and Perspectives
segments.why: The conclusions summarize earlier contributions and constitute back matter rather than a new source of design detail.

segments.title: Bibliography
segments.why: The bibliography contains citations rather than chapter-level arithmetic-unit descriptions.
